# D07 explicit local Intent — design and source ownership

The P32 producer binding is the existing `CanvasEditingRuntime` internal C++ owner. The planned private-to-the-product Runtime interface is `beginExplicitIntent`, `prepareExplicitIntent`, `commitExplicitIntent`, `abortExplicitIntent`, with a target-private explicit-intent context. These are P32 obligations, not existing methods or proof of behavior. A real in-process consumer/test calls this production owner; they must not be added to the product's C ABI or to platform/UI code. If exact names need an internal equivalent, retain a documented one-to-one binding and rerun the same real-owner oracle.

## Lifecycle

`begin` creates one private, owner-thread-bound local intent context containing identity, document and semantic-generation basis, ordered typed candidates, and diagnostics. It is not an Operation or wire value. It does not mutate canonical state, History or Scene, and no implicit group is created from separate calls. The context cannot cross a long gesture, await user input or cross a public ABI boundary.

`prepare` validates identity, document, support, duplicate/colliding Operation IDs and limits; stages the ordered sequence against successive staged states through the real Semantic planner; prepares exact inverse Operations in reverse order and per-target expectations, forward/inverse payload limits, and redo intent; allocates/reserves all History, actual per-Operation store/index/ledger/ChangeSet/result/publication storage and required generation/ordinal capacity. Failure destroys the context with no canonical mutation, no successful History item, no cursor/redo/Scene/observer change. Selection changes do not alter captured targets. Stale basis causes reprepare or pre-write rejection.

`commit` enters a short same-document ordered Runtime lane; revalidates basis/admission and performs the already prepared per-Operation writes without interleaving and without a recoverable failure after the first mutation. On whole success, install one reserved History entry without allocation, then deliver the coherent local result. Each real Operation retains its own ID, generation, stamp and ChangeSet, with eligible DataBridge notifications in canonical order; Scene/observers cannot expose a partial failed intent. If preserving those per-Operation obligations and coherent visibility cannot be demonstrated simultaneously, stop as an Authority/design conflict rather than silently coalescing publications. Do not hold the lane for gesture, input, database, network, rendering or presentation.

`abort` is valid only before the first canonical mutation: destroy provisional storage and leave Document, History cursor/redo, Scene and observer state unchanged. Once canonical writes begin, do not pretend abort rewinds canonical metadata. Unexpected prefix failures must be surfaced according to `closure.md`; normal 07-14 compensation is not proof of D07's pre-mutation rejection. After success the context is consumed exactly once.

Undo/Redo enter the same real owner path with captured target expectations, inverse reverse ordering, and freshly allocated Operation IDs. Prevalidate and reserve each group before writing. One successful Undo reverses the entire intent; Redo recreates its forward meaning using fresh IDs, independently of current selection. Existing standalone single-operation History semantics stay intact.

## Existing source seams and work required

| Source owner | Current fact at source revision | Required P32 work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime/interaction/include/canvas/interaction/editor_history.hpp`; `src/editor_history.cpp` | `PreparedEntry` has one forward; `executeUndoable` and admitted `submitFresh` accept one; cursor reservation exists | Retain ordered exact forwards/inverses and expectations as one existing-owner History entry; preserve ordinary entry semantics and fresh IDs. |
| `runtime/interaction/src/undoable_command.hpp/.cpp` | `prepareUndoableCommand` derives a single real inverse and measures actual protobuf payload | Extend private preparation to sequential staged context and reverse correctness, without reproducing a weak semantic validator. |
| `runtime/interaction/include/canvas/interaction/canvas_editing_runtime.hpp`; `src/canvas_editing_runtime.cpp` | `submitAdmitted` takes one Operation; span submit rejects multi-op; `observeApplied` copies a commit record after canonical write inside `noexcept` | Own the explicit producer and lane, guard reentrancy/external apply, reserve and install results before publication, retain Scene recovery; preserve legacy span rejection. |
| `runtime/semantic/src/operation_engine.cpp`, `atomic_apply.cpp`, `indexed_object_store.cpp`, `object_store_mutator.hpp`, `applied_operation_ledger.cpp`, `change_set_builder.cpp`, `object_index.cpp` and their specified existing headers | `OperationEngine::apply` prepares/reserves one Operation, and `atomic_apply` constructs allocating preflight sets and `prepareContainerPlan` at each call; ledger reservation and clock successors are per-call | Only where required, expose private no-fail prepared per-Operation machinery to the existing owners, staged for dependencies and fully reserved before first write. Do not invent a global transaction or change semantics for existing calls. |
| `runtime/scene/src/incremental_runtime_coordinator.cpp` | Existing Scene publication/recovery owner | Reuse it; no Scene source change authorized absent a separately justified scope correction. |

The current per-Operation code is **not** a no-fail group commit. Pre-reserving only `EditorHistory::entries_` or only an inverse vector does not reserve ObjectStore/index, ledger, ChangeSet, commit-record copy, generation/ordinal space and publication. A P31 design pass establishes a bounded implementation route, not proof that route already works; P32 must provide executable evidence. If the exact sources/ABI constraints make the guarantee unimplementable within the allowed surface, stop with concrete owner/path and no unsafe workaround.

The earlier D07 user acceptance and targeted current record require failure before canonical mutation. The 07-14 integration contract separately describes per-Operation outputs and compensation for unexpected middle failures. The implementation must not use compensation to relabel a mutated prefix as zero mutation; preserve both facts and escalate a demonstrated mismatch. PHYS, cross-client/crash atomicity and D06-B are not closed by this package.
